🇺🇸 TRUMP JUST PUT A SPOTLIGHT ON THE DOWNSTREAM RESULTS OF THE USAID TAKEDOWN…

President Trump just amplified Donald Trump Jr.’s observation:

Since USAID was gutted, the left has not won a single one of the presidential elections being cited across Latin America.

Think about the implications of that correlation.

For years what gets called foreign aid, democracy promotion, civil society funding and NGO assistance was in many cases actually infrastructure capable of shaping another country’s political environment.

And here’s the part people forget:

The people who created this system essentially acknowledged where the model came from.

Allen Weinstein, one of the founders of the National Endowment for Democracy, famously said in 1991:

“A lot of what we do today was done covertly 25 years ago by the CIA.”

That wasn’t some anonymous conspiracy theorist.

That was one of the architects of the democracy-promotion establishment.

USAID’s own documents are equally revealing about the scope of these programs.

They funded or supported:

• Political-party development
• Election organizations and processes
• NGOs and civil-society organizations
• “Independent” media
• Civic and voter education
• Electoral-law reform
• Political participation programs
• The electoral “information environment”
• Post-election political transitions

USAID formally insisted that these programs were impartial and were not designed to determine election outcomes. But research suggests otherwise. 

If you’re financing the political parties, activist organizations, media ecosystem, voter-engagement apparatus and civil-society infrastructure surrounding an election, how meaningful is the distinction between influencing the political environment and influencing its eventual outcome?

Now look at what happened.

The Trump administration dismantles enormous portions of that foreign-aid infrastructure.

The funding pipeline is disrupted.

And suddenly we get this extraordinary sequence of Latin American elections in which the political left repeatedly fails to win.

When you already have decades of documentation showing that American government money was deliberately being used to shape foreign political institutions—and one of the architects of the system openly compared it to activities previously conducted covertly by the CIA—the correlation deserves serious scrutiny.

And perhaps the most interesting development today:

President Trump himself is now drawing public attention to that exact correlation.

That is the signal.

For years the debate was:

“Was American foreign aid really political influence masquerading as humanitarian assistance?”

Now Trump is effectively pointing people toward the results and saying:

Look at what changed after the money stopped.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian and Russian President Vladimir Putin stressed the need to maintain and strengthen bilateral and strategic cooperation between Tehran and Moscow during a phone call on Wednesday.

Pezeshkian congratulated Putin on his birthday and wished Russia and its people continued growth, prosperity and success. He also highlighted the positive and expanding trend in relations between the two countries and the importance of continuing cooperation across various fields.
​
Putin thanked Pezeshkian for his birthday wishes and expressed hopes for peace, prosperity, security and success for Iran and its people.
​
The Russian president said Tehran-Moscow cooperation under their comprehensive strategic partnership treaty was continuing despite ongoing developments and events in the region.
​
Putin also highlighted the historic resilience of the Iranian people in the face of attacks, saying Iran’s courage had drawn attention and admiration internationally.
​
The two presidents also discussed diplomatic efforts by some countries to reduce tensions in the region. Putin said Russia supported such initiatives and was ready to assist efforts aimed at easing tensions.
